seoTitle: How to Hide Active Status on Instagram (Turn Off Active Now) 2026
metaDescription: Turn off Show activity status on Instagram so the green dot and "Active now" label disappear — same steps on iPhone and Android, plus what it doesn't hide.
intro: The green dot beside your name in Instagram DMs quietly tells everyone you've ever messaged exactly when you're on your phone. Switching it off takes about fifteen seconds once you know the setting is called Show activity status and lives under Messages and story replies, not anywhere obviously labelled privacy. The steps are the same on iPhone and Android because the setting lives on your account, not the device. This guide covers where to find it, the trade-off Instagram makes you accept in exchange, and Instagram's own wording for that trade-off, which is stricter than most people assume.

steps.heading: See what other people currently see
steps.body: Open your DM inbox from the paper-plane icon and look at the rows. Anyone whose activity status is on shows a green dot beside their profile picture and the words Active now under their name; people who've been offline a while show a last-seen note like "Sent on Friday" instead. That's exactly how your own row looks in everyone else's inbox right now. Checking here first gives you an obvious before-and-after: come back to this screen once you've flipped the setting, and your own dot will be gone from other people's view.

image.caption: The Instagram DM inbox, where one contact shows a green dot and "Active now" while the others show only when they last sent something.

steps.heading: Open Settings and privacy
steps.body: Tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner, then the three-line menu at the top right, and choose Settings and privacy. The list is long and grouped under headings: How you use Instagram covers Saved, Archive, Your activity, Notifications and Time management; Who can see your content holds Account privacy, Close Friends, Crossposting, Blocked and Hide story and live; and below that, How others can interact with you begins with Messages and story replies. Activity status sits in that last group, not in Who can see your content, which is where most people look first and give up.

image.caption: Settings and privacy, with Messages and story replies at the start of the "How others can interact with you" group.

steps.heading: Jump straight to Show activity status
steps.body: Instead of scrolling, use the search box at the top of Settings and privacy and type a few letters of "show"; Show activity status comes up as the first result. This shortcut is worth remembering generally: Instagram reorganizes this menu often enough that written directions go stale while the search stays reliable. If you'd rather navigate manually, the setting sits inside Messages and story replies. Either way you land on the same screen.

image.caption: Typing into the settings search box surfaces Show activity status as the first match.

steps.heading: Turn the toggle off
steps.body: The Show activity status screen has a single toggle with a line of explanatory text underneath. Blue means on, the default; tapping it turns it grey. There's no Save button and no confirmation. The change applies immediately across your account, on every device you're logged into, and for everyone you've ever chatted with. Turning it back on later is the same tap, and Instagram doesn't tell anyone that you changed it either way.

steps.heading: Accept the trade-off it makes
steps.body: Instagram enforces this trade-off symmetrically, and its own help documentation spells it out directly: once you turn off your activity status, you stop seeing when anyone you follow or message is active, was recently active, or is active in the same chat as you, and they lose the same view of you. There's no setting that hides your status while keeping visibility into everyone else's. If seeing when a particular person is online matters to you, weigh that against your own privacy, because you can't have both.

steps.heading: Know what it doesn't hide
steps.body: Turning off activity status covers the green dot and the Active now and recently-active labels. It doesn't make you invisible elsewhere: read receipts still show a Seen marker when you open someone's message, your name still appears in the viewer list of any story you watch, and your own story stays visible to whoever your account privacy allows. For anything broader than the online indicator, look separately at Account privacy for who can follow you, Hide story and live for specific people, and Restrict or Block for individual accounts. Activity status is one narrow switch, not a privacy mode.

faq.question: Where is the Active now setting on Instagram?
faq.answer: Profile, then the three-line menu, then Settings and privacy. Search for "show activity status", or open Messages and story replies and find it there. It is not under the Who can see your content group.

faq.question: Is the process different on iPhone and Android?
faq.answer: No. Show activity status is an account setting, not a device one, so the path is the same in both apps and the change applies everywhere you're logged in.

faq.question: Will I still see when other people are active?
faq.answer: No. Instagram's help documentation confirms the trade-off is mutual: turning off your own status also removes your ability to see everyone else's, including who's active, recently active, or in the same chat as you.

faq.question: Does hiding activity status also hide when I've read a message?
faq.answer: No. Read receipts are separate, so the sender still sees a Seen marker when you open their message. The toggle only affects the online and recently-active indicators.

faq.question: Does anyone get notified when I turn it off?
faq.answer: No notification is sent. Your dot simply stops appearing, and someone would have to be watching your row in their inbox closely to notice the change.
